creates_law_reviewed.class: LAW -- a general no-go generalising B1203's zero cut from one symmetry to every symmetry readable off the object
creates_law_reviewed.basis: read at banking: the product is a structural impossibility argument closing the programme's most-cited open item

claim_one_line: NOTHING IS HIDING: NO SYMMETRY READABLE OFF THE OBJECT CAN SELECT WITHIN ITS OWN CANONICAL CLASS (owner's question: what is hiding that would force the top breakthrough and solve everything downstream). THE STANDING OPEN ITEM: MENU-1 showed the value arm cannot be won by value-matching -- 11,720 type-respecting maps, median gap 3.53e-5, min 1.63e-9 -- and concluded it 'needs a forcing theorem that selects one map before looking; that theorem does not exist; it is new mathematics, and it is the single thing standing between the programme and a computed SM number'. THE ARGUMENT, five steps each citing a banked result: (1) B1168's parity-times-dimension law, object-canonical iff beta-even AND dimensionless; (2) MENU-1/B1203, the 17 tier-1 atoms are object-canonical and every menu value is built from them by {+,-,*,/,sqrt}; (3) GC-15/B1191, the admissible group is G = Stab_Aut(D)|_T READ OFF D and never chosen, which is the whole content of 'expressible from the object'; (4) an Aut(D)-invariant is fixed by every subgroup of Aut(D), hence by G; (5) those operations are G-equivariant, so G fixes every atom and hence EVERY menu value. CONCLUSION: G acts TRIVIALLY -- all 11,720 are fixed points. GC-15 regime (i) requires G TRANSITIVE to give a unique invariant measure and a log2|T| cost; a trivial action is the opposite extreme, every subset invariant, no measure distinguished, no selection possible. THE RESULT: the cut is zero for EVERY symmetry readable off the object, for the same reason B1203 found it zero for c -- 'the menu lies wholly inside the c-even class already; requiring what every candidate satisfies selects nothing' -- and that reason is not special to c, because invariance cannot distinguish among invariants. So the missing forcing theorem is not missing; it is IMPOSSIBLE IN THE FORM SOUGHT, by a one-line consequence of the programme's own law. WHY THIS ANSWERS RATHER THAN DODGES: the rows are not stuck for want of a discovery but for one shared provable reason, and once stated every row follows -- MENU-1's maps (canonical, G-trivial, no selection); the CS bit {0,1/4} (beta-ODD, so the reader's by B1168); family/VEV and the colour frame (an invariant selector cannot pick a point of its own orbit); P^3 (compact, GC-15 regime ii, a canonical PRIOR but never a point); ell and sigma (non-compact, regime iii, prior-vs-point ill-typed); lambda (B721, the modular flow is trivial, nothing to read off). ONE LAW, SIX ROWS. CLOSES: the search for a forcing theorem built from the object's own symmetries -- over, by proof rather than exhaustion, and it explains why two years of value-matching produced ten honest negatives. DOES NOT CLOSE: whether a selector exists using data that is NOT an object-invariant; B1168 types such data as beta-odd or dimensionful, i.e. the reader's column, where this argument does not forbid one -- the Heartbeat Atlas's thesis reached from the opposite direction. FENCE: step 2 rests on the atoms being object-canonical, which is MENU-1's own construction rule, cited not re-derived (cloud's enumerator is primary). Gate 5 clean.
